text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois are targeted by recurring local and digital scams, including fake government text messages, door-to-door contractor fraud after severe weather, and online shopping traps. The [Better Business Bureau serving Central Illinois](bbb.org bureau-serving-central-illinois-and-western-illinois) and the Illinois Attorney General actively track these deceptive schemes.

list.snippet: What happens: You receive a text message claiming to be from the Illinois Secretary of State, the DMV, or an unearned toll violation. The text says your driver's license will be suspended or you face legal penalties unless you click a link to pay immediately.
Why it fails/works: It creates panic over essential driving privileges. However, state agencies never request immediate fine payments or personal details via unprompted text messages.
Action: Do not click any links or enter personal information. Verify any actual vehicle or license status directly through official state portals.

What happens: Following severe storms common across the Midwest, transient contractors ("stormchasers") knock on doors offering cheap, immediate roof repairs or free damage inspections. They pressure homeowners for large upfront cash deposits and often disappear before doing the work.

Why it fails/works: They exploit urgency and a desire to fix home damage quickly. Legitimate local contractors provide physical business addresses, licenses, and written contracts without high-pressure cash demands.
Action: Never sign an agreement on the spot. Get multiple written estimates, verify local licensing, and avoid paying large sums in cash before work is completed and inspected.

What happens: Scammers send texts disguised as USPS, UPS, or general delivery carriers claiming a package cannot be delivered due to a missing house number or unpaid shipping fee, prompting you to click a link.

Why it fails/works:
With frequent online shopping, recipients easily mistake the fake notification for a real order.
Action: Check the tracking number inside the official carrier app or website rather than clicking links embedded in text messages.

text_blocks.snippet: 💻 ➡️ Fake Online Retail and Holiday Web Ads

list.snippet: What happens: Professional-looking social media ads or search engine results promote deep discounts on trending electronics, hard-to-find toys, or luxury goods. Entering payment details results in stolen credit card information and no delivered product.
Why it fails/works: Prices look too good to be true. These pop-up sites often lack functional customer service contacts, clear return policies, or secure checkout features.
Action: Research unfamiliar online merchants via the Better Business Bureau before purchasing, and use credit cards which offer stronger fraud protection than debit cards.

text_blocks.snippet:
If you encounter or fall victim to a scam in Central Illinois, report it immediately to the Illinois Attorney General Consumer Fraud Hotline or file a report with the
Better Business Bureau Scam Tracker to alert neighbors in your community
.

If you've been targeted by a specific type of scam or received a suspicious message, tell me how they contacted you (text, phone, or email) and what they asked for so I can help you verify if it's fraudulent.
